title: Interpretable, Fairly Evaluated Automated L2 Speaking Assessment that Beats the Single-Human Ceiling and Why Pause Encoding Does Not Change LLM Fluency Scores
abstract: arXiv:2608.26137v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Second-language (L2) English learners can rarely rehearse speaking with a partner. Speaking is also the most anxiety-laden skill. These gaps drive a fast-growing market for automated speaking practice and scoring. But an automated score is trustworthy only if it is accurate, interpretable, fair, and benchmarked against the right human bar. We build an interpretable feature-plus-LLM hybrid for spontaneous L2 dialogue. We evaluate it without ever fitting to the human labels, against the ICNALE Global Rating Archive: 140 speeches rated by ~80 trained raters on 10 analytic criteria. We score the 130 L2 speeches with usable audio. A deterministic De-Jong speech-timing composite reaches rho=0.764. Blended with a single text-LLM fluency judgment, it reaches Spearman rho=0.818 against the consensus gold. translated_title: 可解释、公平评估的自动L2口语评估，超越单人人类评分上限，以及为什么停顿编码不改变LLM流利度评分
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26137v1 公告类型：新公告 摘要：第二语言（L2）英语学习者很少能与伙伴练习口语。口语也是焦虑感最强的技能。这些差距推动了自动化口语练习和评分市场的快速增长。但自动化评分只有在准确、可解释、公平，并针对正确的人类基准进行测评时才值得信赖。我们构建了一个可解释的特征加LLM混合模型，用于自发L2对话。我们从未拟合人类标签，而是针对ICNALE全球评分档案进行评估：140段演讲由约80名训练有素的评分者按10项分析标准评分。我们对130段具有可用音频的L2演讲进行评分。一个确定性的De-Jong语音时间复合指标达到rho=0.764。与单一文本LLM流利度判断混合后，针对共识金标准达到Spearman rho=0.818。这比80名个体训练评分者中81%的共识一致性更好：高于中位评分者（rho=0.73）并接近最佳，且在此水平上。
tldr: 该论文提出一种可解释的特征与LLM混合模型，在L2口语自动评分中超越单人人类评分中位数，实现高准确度和公平性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an interpretable feature-plus-LLM hybrid model that surpasses the median human rater in L2 speaking assessment, achieving high accuracy and fairness.
